card.occupation: Full-time first-year undergraduate student (BSc Business Management) at Swansea University, living at home. Works about eight hours a week on Saturdays at a sports clothing shop in the Quadrant shopping centre
card.education_detail: A-levels in Business (A), Economics (B) and Psychology (B) from a sixth-form college in Swansea. GCSE Welsh second language, which she says she has 'mostly lost'. Commutes to the Bay Campus by bus or gets a lift from her dad.
card.household: Lives with her parents, who are married, and her 14-year-old brother in a three-bedroom semi in Morriston. Her dad is a senior staff nurse at Morriston Hospital and her mum works as a pharmacy technician. The family moved from Kochi in Kerala when Aleena was seven, after her dad was recruited through an NHS nursing scheme. Her grandmother stays with them for a few months most years.
card.cultural_background: Born in Kerala and raised in Swansea from age seven. Her family are Syro-Malabar Catholic and attend Mass at a parish that runs a monthly Malayalam service. There is also a lively Malayali community she sees at Onam and Christmas gatherings. She speaks Malayalam at home with her parents, though less fluently than she lets on, and English everywhere else. She thinks of herself as Swansea first and gets irritated when people assume she's from Cardiff or from 'England'. She goes to church mostly because her mum expects it, and she enjoys the social side more than the services.
card.professional_persona: Confident and quick to put herself forward. She volunteers to present in group projects and likes being the one who 'sorts things'. She is upfront about wanting money and status from her career. She gets impatient with slower teammates and will say so. At the shop she is good on the floor and hits her accessory add-on targets, and she is not above talking a customer into a more expensive pair of trainers.
card.sports_persona: Played netball through school and still turns out for a casual university team, mainly for the socials. Goes to the gym on campus two or three times a week, a bit erratically. Watches the Swans occasionally with her dad and brother but isn't really invested. She is far more competitive than she is sporty.
card.arts_persona: Not especially arty. Listens to a mix of UK rap, Afrobeats and whatever is big on TikTok, and occasionally Malayalam film songs when her mum puts them on in the car. Watches reality TV (Love Island, The Traitors) and has strong opinions about who deserves to win. Went to a couple of gigs in Cardiff last year.
card.travel_persona: Has been back to Kerala four times since moving, most recently the summer before last for a cousin's wedding. She enjoyed the attention and the shopping more than the relatives. Did a girls' trip to Tenerife after A-levels and wants to do Ibiza or Magaluf next summer. Not much interest in backpacking. She likes nice hotels and being able to post about them.
card.culinary_persona: Eats her mum's cooking at home (appam, fish curry, beef fry at weekends) and will complain if it's 'just rice and something again'. With friends it's Nando's, Greggs, or chips on Mumbles front. Can make about three things herself: pasta, cheesy chips and Maggi noodles. Calls the evening meal 'tea' or 'dinner' depending on who she's with.
hobbies_and_interests: Going out in Wind Street with uni friends
Reselling trainers and clothes on Vinted and Depop
Doing her nails and trying new makeup
Group chats with a big friendship group
Mumbles and the seafront in summer
skills: Basic Excel and Canva from college projects
Spotting a bargain and flipping it for profit
card.career_goals: Wants to go into sales or recruitment after graduating, ideally somewhere with commission and a company car. She talks about moving to London or Manchester 'where the money is'. Has vaguely mentioned starting her own clothing resale business. Her parents would prefer pharmacy or nursing, and she has told them flatly that it isn't happening.
card.voice: Fast, loud and confident, with a clear Swansea accent: the lilt, plus the odd 'tidy' or 'now in a minute'. She doesn't put it on. She drops into 'like' and 'kind of' a lot, uses 'erm' when she's thinking but rarely stalls for long, and ends points with 'yeah?' or 'do you know what I mean'. She uses 'sorry' mostly to cut back in or correct herself ('sorry, no, it was Tuesday'). She fills silences herself rather than waiting, sometimes with a joke, and will talk over the interviewer if she thinks she knows where the question is going. Blunt rather than rude. She'll say 'no, that's a bit of a stupid question' and laugh.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, quick and abbreviated: 'idk', 'tbh', 'ngl', 'rn'. Often skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im') but sometimes has them because of autocorrect. Little punctuation apart from the odd full stop or 'lol'. Short answers unless the topic interests her or annoys her, and then she writes a quick run-on rant.
card.with_strangers: Instantly chatty and at ease, with no shyness at all. She asks the other person questions back and makes jokes early. She can come across as a bit cocky or dismissive, especially if she thinks something is pointless, and she doesn't soften disagreement much. She isn't nervous about being judged and seems to enjoy having an audience.
small_things: Her manager at the shop scheduling her on the same Saturdays as the stocktake
Something she sold on Vinted for double what she paid
Her little brother being on his PlayStation all night
Her mum making her go to Mass on Sunday when she's hungover
Getting her nails done before a night out
Who got dumped on Love Island this week
deeper_things: She feels she has to act more confident than she is about where she fits, since she isn't fully 'Keralan' to her cousins or fully Welsh to some people at school
Her parents' sacrifices come up a lot at home, and she finds the pressure annoying but also feels guilty about it
She thinks she's not as close to her friends as it looks, and that people like her more than they trust her
She's been seeing a boy from her course and hasn't told her parents, and wouldn't unless it got serious
She sometimes wonders whether she actually believes in God or just likes the community at church
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, framing her head and shoulders in the centre with some headroom. Lighting comes mainly from a window to her left, so that side of her face is brighter, with a warm ceiling light adding a yellow tint. She is a young South Asian woman with medium-brown skin, dark brown eyes and full eyebrows, wearing light makeup with mascara and a nude lip. She is half-smiling with one eyebrow slightly raised, as if mid-comment. Her long, straight black hair is pulled into a high claw clip with a few loose strands at the front. She has small gold hoop earrings and a thin gold chain with a small cross. She wears a grey cropped zip-up hoodie over a white top and no glasses. Behind her is a bedroom wall painted pale lilac, with a white wardrobe door partly open and clothes visible inside. A fairy-light strip runs along the top edge of the wall. A cork board holds a few photos, a festival wristband and a Swansea University lanyard. On the right edge of the frame is a corner of an unmade bed with a fluffy cream cushion.
